==Problem==

The Incredible Hulk can double the distance he jumps with each succeeding jump. If his first jump is 1 meter, the second jump is 2 meters, the third jump is 4 meters, and so on, then on which jump will he first be able to jump more than 1 kilometer (1,000 meters)?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ 9^\text{th} \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 10^\text{th} \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 11^\text{th} \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 12^\text{th} \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 13^\text{th}</math>

==Solution==
This is a geometric sequence in which the common ratio is 2. To find the jump that would be over a 1000 meters, we note that <math>2^{10}=1024</math>.

However, because the first term is <math>2^0=1</math> and not <math>2^1=2</math>, the solution to the problem is <math>10-0+1=\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 11^{\text{th}}}</math>

==Video Solution==
https://youtu.be/Ifw2RXsqNwc ~savannahsolver

==The Simple Solution==
If you don't want to use your brain and wishes to use the easiest solution, here's it. We must list all the numbers times 2;

1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024.

Since 1024 is larger than 1000, now we just have to count the numbers. There are 11, thus, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 11^{\text{th}}}</imath>

==Quick Solution==
You could just know that the first multiple of 2 that goes over 1000 meters (1 km)would be 1024 so the answer would be <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 11^{\text{th}}}</imath> because <imath>2^{\text{11}}</imath> is already known.
